sections.body:
- Project ID: `deepseek-harness`
- Canonical name: DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`) (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-identity`)
- Vendor: README `DeepSeek AI` (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-vendor`); LICENSE copyright `DeepSeek` (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-vendor-license`)
- Current status: developer preview; compatibility-breaking changes expected (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-status`, `claim-deepseek-harness-sf-status-breaking`)
- Last source-backed identity check: 2026-08-15
- Canonical URL: https://www.deepseek.com/harness/en/ (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-canonical-url`)
- Public repository: https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-repository-url`)
- Workspace version on this check: `0.1.0-rc.5` (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-version`); GitHub Releases listed none (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-version-releases`)

sections.heading: What it is and is not
sections.body:
- What it is: DeepSeek AI's open-source plugin-based agent harness (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-what-it-is`, `claim-deepseek-harness-sf-vendor`)
- What it is not: a managed-cloud agent product or a first-party desktop IDE download on opened pages (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-what-it-is-not`)
- Distinct from `deepseek-reasonix` (Reasonix / esengine / reasonix.io) (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-not-reasonix`)
- Distinct from `codewhale` (community product formerly named DeepSeek TUI) (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-not-codewhale`)

sections.heading: Architecture and agent-loop ownership
sections.body:
- Primary type: `runtime` as a project classification of the cited architecture docs (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-primary-type`)
- Agent-loop owner: DeepSeek Harness first-party loop plugin (`core/agent-loop`, `ctx.agentLoop`); the loop is itself replaceable (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-agent-loop`)
- Architecture: official page built on Cordis; everything is a plugin (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-architecture`); README powered by Cordis (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-architecture-powered-by-cordis`); architecture docs name the model adapter, tool registry, session log, and agent loop as plugins (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-architecture-plugin-parts`); Cordis is vendored under `vendor/` (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-architecture-vendored`)
- Shipped profiles: `web` and `headless` over `dsh-base` (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-profiles`)
- Runtime modes, not access surfaces: Standard, Code, Minimal, Creator (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-modes`)

sections.heading: Surfaces and execution location
sections.body:
- Surface IDs: `surface-deepseek-harness-web`, `surface-deepseek-harness-cli-headless`, `surface-deepseek-harness-python-sdk`
- Execution location: user-controlled local workspace (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-execution-location`); Python SDK caller-supplied workspace (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-execution-location-python-sdk`)

sections.heading: Model/auth/provider strategy
sections.body:
- Model strategy: DeepSeek-first Settings → Models path, plus catalog, native-auth, and custom OpenAI-compatible providers; a session keeps the model already recorded in its log (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-model-strategy`)
- Auth strategy: BYOK keys in `$DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml` or a referenced environment variable; native providers use AWS credentials, ADC, `api-version`, or OAuth (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-auth-strategy`); Python SDK reads `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` and optional `DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL` (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-auth-strategy-sdk-env`)
- Provider support: named examples are DeepSeek, Anthropic, OpenAI, Bedrock, Vertex, Azure, Codex, and custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-provider-support`)

sections.heading: Context, memory, compaction, and session behavior
sections.body:
- Context behavior: append-only session log is the model-visible context (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-context`); architecture docs add model-visible means logged (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-context-model-visible`)
- Memory: storage is named as a plugin capability; a dedicated conversation-memory product is unknown (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-memory`); cookbook maps Memory to a section provider plus tool (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-memory-cookbook`)
- Compaction: optional `ctx.compaction` seam; not part of the agent-loop spine (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-compaction`); checked-in Python SDK example disables compaction (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-compaction-sdk-disabled`)
- Session behavior: resume, fork, search, and replay on the same event stream; Trajectory view inspects records by source (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-session`); `ctx.sessions.fork` creates a live child from a stable prefix (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-session-fork-api`)

sections.heading: Tools, extensions, MCP, skills, hooks, and APIs
sections.body:
- Tools: Standard is the full coding-agent toolset; Minimal is persistent bash plus `str_replace_editor`; Code exposes tools through the Code Mode SDK (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-tools`)
- Extensions: Cordis plugins, swappable from configuration; community topic `dsh-plugin` (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-extensions`)
- MCP: cookbook maps MCP to one plugin per server; no first-party MCP settings UI on opened user guides (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-mcp`)
- Skills: plugin capability included in Standard mode (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-skills`); cookbook maps Skills to section plus tool with `inject()` on invocation (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-skills-cookbook`)
- Hooks: native hook plugins plus Claude Code and Codex hook bridges (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-hooks`)
- APIs: published Python SDK (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-api`). A published JSON-RPC product API is unknown.

sections.heading: Orchestration and parallelism
sections.body:
- Orchestration: Code mode orchestrates multi-step tool calls; Standard adds planning, goals, subagents, and workflows (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-orchestration`); cookbook maps `/goal`, Dynamic workflow, and Sub-agent delegation onto plugin mechanisms (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-orchestration-cookbook`)
- Parallelism: subagent scheduling is first-party; agent teams unknown (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-parallelism`); cookbook names in-process, fork, acp, codex, claude-code, and dsh-sdk subagent providers (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-parallelism-providers`)

sections.heading: Isolation, permissions, security, and data path
sections.body:
- Isolation: landlock / sandbox-exec through `dsh-bash-sandbox` (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-isolation`); Windows ACL restricted-token runner (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-isolation-windows-acl`)
- Permissions: Web UI asks before operations that require approval (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-permissions`); cookbook maps permission / AskUserQuestion to `tools/pre-execute` ask plus `ctx.approval` (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-permissions-cookbook`)
- Security: the published Python example uses `danger-full-access` and should run only in a disposable checkout or container (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-security`)
- Data path: local `$DSH_HOME` credentials; model calls go to the configured provider (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-data-path`); Python SDK writes JSONL under the caller session root (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-data-path-sdk-jsonl`)

sections.body:
Modes Standard, Code, Minimal, and Creator are runtime compositions, not extra surfaces (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-modes`).

- Interface and surface IDs:
  - Local Web UI: `surface-deepseek-harness-web` (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-surface-web`, `claim-deepseek-harness-sf-surface-web-cli-alias`, `claim-deepseek-harness-sf-surface-web-bind`)

- Remote behavior: local loopback is documented; all-interfaces bind is rejected; first-party remoting unknown (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-remote-access`). Web UI `remote_start` and Python SDK `remote_resume` stay unknown.
- Mobile behavior: unknown (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-mobile-access`)
- Background behavior: scheduling is a named plugin capability; a first-party cloud background agent is unknown (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-background`); architecture docs register background work on `ctx.jobs` (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-background-jobs`)
- First-party messaging: unknown (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-mobile-access`)

- First-party mobile web: unknown (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-mobile-access`)

sections.heading: Pricing, license, maintenance, and lock-in
sections.body:
- Pricing: no harness seat price on the official page; distribution is `npx` or source clone (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-pricing`); model use is user-supplied provider keys (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-pricing-byok`)
- License: MIT (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-license`)
- Maintenance: early-stage active development; external PRs not accepted (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-maintenance`)
- Lock-in: swappable plugins and evolving APIs (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-lock-in`); MIT (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-lock-in-mit`); DeepSeek-first defaults (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-lock-in-deepseek-first`); compatibility-breaking changes (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-lock-in-breaking`)
- Availability: Node.js `npx` / source (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-availability`); Node engines (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-availability-node-engines`); Python SDK on Linux and macOS arm64 (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-availability-python-sdk`); Windows pwsh path documented (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-availability-windows-pwsh`)

sections.heading: Unique edge, meaningful drawbacks, best fit, and not-for
sections.body:
- Unique edge: plugin kernel, reconstructable session log, and four documented runtime modes (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-unique`)
- Meaningful drawbacks: developer preview and compatibility-breaking changes (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-drawback`); evolving core plugins and APIs (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-drawback-evolve`); closed external PRs (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-maintenance`)
- Best fit: documented audience is agent harness developers (`claim-deepseek-harness-sf-intended-user`). This is not a recommendation.
